RETRACTION: An earlier version of repro_threading_2026-09-13.json and TRANSFER_WALL section 13 concluded from TWO disagreeing runs that the fit is nondeterministic because of multithreaded float reduction order. Four further replicates refute that: five post-refactor runs at four threads are bitwise identical on every arm and every benchmark. The fit is DETERMINISTIC. Two runs cannot distinguish nondeterminism from two deterministic code paths; the single-threaded control was consistent with the threading hypothesis but did not discriminate between them.
VERDICT: Six runs give TWO answers, not six. The five post-refactor runs agree bitwise; the sixth is the pre-refactor run that produced the shipped +0.0736. The gap reaches 0.0029 and every per-benchmark value differs. Cause still open: the refactor, or the earlier run's thread count, which its log did not record (CLAUDE.md prices a thread-count change at +0.0048, larger than this gap). What is already settled regardless: the shipped choice of pooled_ens over pooled_ens_sc (+0.0016) is not robust -- on five of six runs pooled_ens_sc is the better arm.
